title: Slimline Reserve Briefing & Burst Quickpanels
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Design a compact, contextual ‘Reserve Briefing’ card and an associated Burst Quickpanels component for the Redwood Console dedicated capacity views. The briefing card gives a one-glance summary of a GPU pool's health, active autoscale policy, recent burst events, and a cost-impact estimate for a proposed burst. The Burst Quickpanel is a lightweight modal/slide-over that exposes safe quick actions (trigger burst, set burst duration, choose burst preset) with inline cost and SLO impact estimates and a confirm flow. This work focuses on microinteractions, keyboard accessibility, clear failure states, and a constrained visual footprint so the components can be embedded in list rows, pool detail sidebars, and mobile/responsive sheets.
acceptance_criteria: Figma prototype with annotated flows for Reserve Briefing card and Burst Quickpanel
Responsive designs for desktop (wide list + sidebar) and narrow view (mobile sheet), with breakpoints listed
Accessibility: keyboard navigation, ARIA labels, contrast checks, and screen reader copy documented
Cost/latency impact widget hooked to telemetry mock endpoints (dev props) and shown in prototype
Handoff artifacts: component tokens, spacing system, copy variants, and dev storybook examples
PM sign-off and at least one engineering feasibility comment from infra team
review_feedback: Liam Chen (PM) - 'Love the one-line cost delta, but add an explicit fallback when telemetry is delayed (show 'estimate pending')'
Rohit Singh (Infra) - 'Quickpanel needs friction guard: require a 10s countdown for bursts > 2x baseline to avoid accidental spikes'
Evelyn Park (Design Lead) - 'Tighten microcopy for accessibility; change 'Burst' CTA to 'Start Burst' to make action verb explicit'
QA note - 'Visual regression tests should include color-blind contrast presets; flag for Storybook snapshot tests'
